notes: Answered strictly from documented public biography of John F. Kennedy (b. 29 May 1917, 3:00 PM, 83 Beals Street, Brookline MA - a home birth; time carried on the birth record, hence 'certificate' and a round-hour precision). No chart, horoscope or planetary reasoning was used or consulted; no verdict/reading files were opened. Key sourcing notes: A6/A7/A8 - scarlet fever at age 2 (near-fatal, 1920), lifelong back trouble, colitis/gastrointestinal disease, Addison's disease (adrenal/endocrine) diagnosed 1947, documented chronic urinary/prostate infections (Dallek's review of the medical records). A9 - grandparents PJ Kennedy 71, Mary Hickey Kennedy 65, John F. 'Honey Fitz' Fitzgerald 87, Mary Josephine Hannon Fitzgerald 98; mean ~80. A13 - Joe Jr. (1944) and Kathleen (1948) both died; Rosemary institutionalised. A15 - Princeton withdrawal through illness in 1935 cost roughly a year before Harvard. A19 - 'above' reflects the Pulitzer for 'Profiles in Courage' (Sorensen's heavy hand) and the PT-109 acclaim against a thin legislative record. A28/A29 - Caroline, John Jr. and Patrick born, plus the 1955 miscarriage, the 1956 stillbirth (Arabella) and Patrick's death at two days in August 1963. A31 - 'brief': documented short courses of Stelazine/antianxiety medication in 1961, no documented extended treatment. A33 - lived abroad (LSE 1935, London 1938-39 as the ambassador's son) as well as decades away from Brookline. A34 - months-long hospitalisations plus boarding school at Choate. A36 is not applicable to a man who died in 1963; 'same' was entered as the least misleading available token. C4 answered with low confidence: Jacqueline Bouvier brought social standing rather than money, the Bouvier fortune having largely gone. Part D was left unanswered on purpose - it asks about a reading this exercise forbade me to open, so any answer would be fabricated.
